supported_claims: The solution method is fifth-order Radau IIA with a third-order embedded error estimator.
Absolute tolerances may be scalar or component arrays.
The dense output uses a cubic collocation polynomial.
primary_sources.claim_limit: Documentation describes local tolerance control, not a certified endpoint error bound for the C21F physical observables.

supported_claims: The endpoint scale uses the component-wise maximum magnitude of the old and new solution.
Acceptance uses the imported norm on the scaled embedded error.
The finite-difference Jacobian receives absolute tolerance as its component threshold.
The norm used by the adaptive solver is root mean square, not maximum norm.
Relative tolerance below 100 machine epsilon is raised by the implementation.
A non-scalar atol must match the dimension of the actual integrated state.
primary_sources.derived_implication: A scalar normalized estimator can reach square root of the dynamic state dimension while the RMS remains at most one; this does not define a component-wise maximum bound.

primary_sources.retrieval: Exa search located the author and institutional originals; Exa fetch read the author PDF through sections 2 and 3
supported_claims: Global error assessment requires information about both discretization perturbations and their amplification by the differential equation.
Adjoint equations can weight residuals for endpoint observables.
Using a nonlinear approximate trajectory introduces a remainder and accuracy assumptions.
primary_sources.claim_limit: The paper supports the error-estimation framework. Its existence does not certify the current native solve or an empirical tolerance ladder.
